summary.text: 分 is traditionally explained as a knife separating things: 刀 depicts the knife, and 八 the things separated. Early forms are also analyzed as giving 八 a sound role, though that proposal is disputed.

formation.text: A semantic compound: 刀 depicts the knife and contributes the act of separation, while 八 is interpreted as depicting the separated things. A separate analysis proposes that 八 also cues the sound; that role remains disputed because the cited comparison is imperfect.

components.text: 八 is interpreted as depicting the two things separated by the knife. One analysis also proposes a phonetic role, but the comparison is imperfect and does not establish that role or its historical mechanism.

sound_limitation.text: A sound comparison is reported, but its imperfect match does not independently establish 八’s identity as a phonetic element in 分 or the historical mechanism.

sound.text: The proposed comparison is between 八 and 分 in the sense “divide.” Mandarin bā and fēn differ; in the Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese system, 八 is *pˤret and 分 is *pə[n], also an imperfect match.

components.text: 刀 depicts the knife in the separation scene; the traditional analysis assigns it a role in expressing separation.

history.text: The selected Shang oracle-script form has marks on either side of 刀. Oracle-bone and bronze forms are reported with 八 and 刀, while Chu manuscript and Small Seal forms are also indexed. These records do not show every intermediate graphic change. The selected image is a modern vector redraw, not an artifact photograph.

The Shuowen Jiezi glosses 分 as “separate” or “distinguish” and explains it through 八 and 刀, with the knife separating things. This historical dictionary account does not independently confirm the graph’s original design.

uncertainties.text: 八 is interpreted as depicting the separated things and is also proposed as a phonetic element. The cited sound comparison is imperfect and does not establish that phonetic role or its historical mechanism.

An oracle-bone place-name use is reported, with a proposed identification near Linfen, but this does not establish the earliest ordinary meaning. The links among separation, allocation, distinction, and quantitative units remain incompletely documented.

senses.text: The Shuowen glosses 分 as “separate” or “distinguish.” This is an attested historical dictionary gloss, not proof that it was the earliest ordinary use; a reported oracle-bone place-name use does not settle that question.

senses.gloss: allocate fields and settlements; allotted duty or status
senses.period: early textual and inscriptional uses; individual dates unresolved
senses.text: An inscription records allocation of fields and settlements, and Warring States manuscript uses are reported for role or status. A separate historical reading is listed for “allotted duty,” but its relationship to the reading for “divide” is not demonstrated.
The Shang Yang measure inscription attests 分 in a fractional measurement expression by 344 BCE. This dates that use, but does not show when it arose or whether it preceded the separation sense.
分 has current senses including “part,” “share,” and “segment.” The available glosses do not establish when these senses arose or a specific path from “separate.”
分 is used for a unit of time. Japanese examples attest that use in 1798–1802, but do not date the corresponding Chinese sense.

developments.text: Allocation may relate to separating or distributing things, but the transition is not directly documented.
A fractional unit may relate to dividing quantities. The dated inscription attests the measurement use, not its development from “separate.”
“Part” can describe what results from separation, but the available evidence does not document this semantic development.
The available evidence records time-unit uses but does not establish whether they developed from fractional measurement or by another route.

limitations.text: The reported oracle-bone place-name use and proposed geographic identification do not establish an ordinary earliest meaning. A complete, dated sequence of semantic developments is not available.
The Japanese attestations establish Japanese uses, but do not establish the chronology of the Chinese character or word.

items.period: Shang dynasty oracle-bone script; approximate broad Shang range as identified on the file page
items.caption: This Shang oracle-script form of 分 places marks on either side of 刀, matching the analysis of a knife separating two things. The early form is also analyzed as having 八 as a phonetic element.
items.alt: Black oracle-script glyph with a central knife-like stroke and two curving strokes on either side.
items.selection_reason: The visible arrangement helps illustrate the separation analysis, while the database account adds a proposed phonetic role for 八. The image alone cannot establish either interpretation.
